messages:
maya: quick heads-up - ran a pprof during a streaming burst. host-side parsing + tokenization is ~40% of host CPU for lots of small requests. flame: https://s3.redwood-internal/profiles/1971237654/host-flame.svg

maya: repro: stress hitting /v1/generate with 64 concurrent 32-token streams over http/1.1. short log below.

maya: ```
[ingress] recv 64 req/s, avg payload 420 bytes
[parse] parse_time_ms p50=0.8 p95=3.4 p99=9.1
[tokenize] p50=1.2 p95=4.6 p99=11.8
[serialize] p50=0.6 p95=2.2
cpu: host-user ~ 42%, kernel ~ 5% (spikes during parse)
```

sam: any diff with grpc/http2? last time chunked paths caused lots of tiny memcpys.

maya: http2/grpc both bad; grpc ~6-8% better on p95. main culprit seems to be full JSON parse + incremental tokenization for tiny payloads.

raj: two quick wins: (1) short header micro-parser for routing so we skip full JSON for known shapes; (2) tokenization offloaded to shared pool workers to reduce alloc churn.

olivia: i +1 the header parser. we used a micro-parser for delta requests before and saved ~0.4ms. also consider coalescing small streaming fragments into a single parse op before tokenization.

maya: prototyped a token buf pool, but saw spinlock contention >128 concurrency.

raj: lock contention expected. try per-shard freelists (shards = cpu/2) + MPMC ring, avoid a global lock. consider jemalloc arena hints to reduce cross-thread fragmentation.

sam: kernel selection hint idea: prefer low-latency kernels for short sequences so host preproc fraction drops and we shift more into GPU fastpath. could advertise via header x-rw-kernel-hint: short-seq.

maya: can we add that header? router already reads some headers. cheap to implement.

raj: ok. i'll add router logic: if short-seq and small payload -> prefer single-stream low-latency kernel.

olivia: streaming chunking tweak: raise min_chunk from 256->1024 for routes with latency budget >50ms to reduce parse overhead. opt-out per-client.

maya: microbench with min_chunk=1024: p95 parse 3.4ms -> 1.9ms, tokenize p95 4.6ms -> 2.8ms. but tiny requests saw +1-2ms first-byte.

sam: make min_chunk configurable per-route and keep PLG default small chunks; enterprise routes default to coalesced.

perf-bot: regression alert — host-parse p95 +12% vs baseline at 1971230000. https://perf.redwood/alerts/1971237654

dev-bot: deploy queued for eng-runtime/shortseq-kernel-hint @maya @raj. CI green. rollout: canary 5% -> 20m -> 50%.

maya: let's opt-in via header in canary to measure before changing kernel selection behavior globally.

raj: PRs incoming: add header + router heuristics, implement per-shard token buf pool, add alloc counters to metrics.

olivia: i'll make min_chunk a route config and add chunk_count metric per request.

sam: when canary numbers land, post p50/p95 host cpu and tokenization timings, plus grpc vs http2 matrix.

maya: canary 5% (10k requests) initial numbers: host-parse p95 down 18%, tokenize p95 down 22%, e2e p95 down 8%. host cpu on canary machines dropped ~10%.

maya: logs: ```
[canary] route: shortseq-hint enabled
[metrics] host_parse_ms_p95: 2.84 -> 2.33
[metrics] tokenize_ms_p95: 4.12 -> 3.21
[notes] tiny clients saw +1-2ms initial latency
```

olivia: great. watch tail noise and retry rates. any subtle regressions for low-latency clients are bad news.

maya: retry rate unchanged so far. monitoring for 6h then bump to 20% if clean.

sam: long-term idea: tiny L1 tokenization cache for repeated short prompts. could help PLG traffic with common prompts.

raj: also instrument per-path kernel selection and correlate host/gpu time. add metrics for kernel_hint usage and token_pool_hits.

maya: PRs: https://git.redwood/eng-runtime/pulls/5483 and https://git.redwood/eng-runtime/pulls/5484

olivia: i'll add dashboard widgets: chunk_count, host_parse_ms_p95, token_pool_hits.

maya: will update after 20% rollout and 6h telemetry. :thumbsup:
